macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Nasdaq rebounds as AI and chip stocks lead Wall Street higher
items.summary: U.S. stocks closed mixed on Monday, with the S&P 500 up 0.4% at 7,690.73 and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.1% at 26,430.89, while the Dow slipped 0.1% to 51,966.03. Semiconductor shares rebounded, led by Micron, Intel, Amazon, Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft and Tesla, as investors positioned ahead of major technology earnings.[1][4]

items.title: Treasury yields rise as markets reassess Federal Reserve rate outlook
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.14% from 5.09% as the technology rebound reduced demand for safe-haven assets. Markets continued pricing a possible December rate increase and higher policy rates next year.[1][3]

items.title: Investors focus on Tesla and Meta earnings
items.summary: Tesla and Meta are scheduled to report later this week, alongside other major technology and semiconductor companies including Lam Research and Texas Instruments. Earnings are expected to provide a key test of artificial-intelligence investment expectations after the sector’s recent sell-off.[2][8]

items.title: Oil remains elevated amid Middle East and Russia supply concerns
items.summary: Brent crude traded around $108–$109 per barrel as attacks affecting tankers and energy infrastructure raised concerns about supply disruptions. Prices remained volatile as investors assessed the outlook for Gulf exports and regional conflict.[2][3]

items.title: China growth improves in the third quarter
items.summary: China’s gross domestic product reportedly grew 4.5% year over year in the third quarter, marking an improvement from recent three-year lows. The data provided a positive macroeconomic signal for Asian markets and global risk sentiment.[6]

items.title: Bank shares underperform after recent earnings
items.summary: U.S. financial stocks declined despite the broader market’s technology-led rebound, with Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Wells Fargo lower following last week’s earnings releases.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $79,000
items.summary: Bitcoin rose 2.17% over 24 hours to about $79,011.60, according to OKX market data. The move came amid broader cryptocurrency-market gains.

items.title: U.S. bill proposes strategic Bitcoin reserve
items.summary: The proposed American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026 would establish a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve at the Treasury and a separate reserve for other digital assets. The legislation was scheduled for review by the House Financial Services Committee.

items.title: Crypto markets rebound as oil prices fall
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1.3% to roughly $82,783, while Ether gained 0.9%, XRP 1.3%, Solana 2%, and BNB 0.9%. The gains followed a decline in oil prices, although markets remained within recent trading ranges.

items.title: Qubic blockchain halted after $1.4 million attack
items.summary: Qubic reportedly paused its blockchain after an attack drained approximately $1.4 million from more than 1,400 wallets. The incident was among the major project-security developments affecting the market.

items.title: Cysic suspends cross-chain bridge after token exploit
items.summary: Cysic halted its cross-chain bridge after an attacker reportedly minted 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Smart Chain. The project subsequently blocked the recipient address.

items.title: Rare solo Bitcoin miner earns 3.147 BTC reward
items.summary: A Braiins Solo miner found Bitcoin block 966351 after nearly 40 days and received the full 3.147 BTC block reward, valued at approximately $244,900 at the time of reporting.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Nvidia launches open-weight models for enterprise and PC AI agents
items.summary: Nvidia introduced the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and lightweight Bolt models for enterprise agents, local AI PCs, and workstations. The company said the models target instruction following, tool use, multistep reasoning, and web browsing, with Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B available immediately.

items.title: MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash AI model
items.summary: Chinese AI startup MiniMax launched M3.1 Flash, claiming major improvements in agentic tasks, programming, and cybersecurity. The company said inference speed nearly tripled while usage costs fell by 70%.

items.title: Research explores hidden-code reasoning for AI agents
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated an approach in which language-model agents alternate between latent internal reasoning and natural-language communication. The method reportedly reduced costs by more than half and accelerated task completion, while raising questions about interpretability.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly completes pre-training of MAI-Base-2
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly finished pre-training its MAI-Base-2 model, described as having 2.8 trillion parameters, and moved the system into post-training. The development signals continued competition among major technology companies to build larger foundation models.

items.title: TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5 becomes available through Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: TwelveLabs’ Pegasus 1.5 video-understanding model is now available through Amazon Bedrock, expanding access to the model through Amazon Web Services’ managed AI platform.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Power to the Players Act would target digital game ownership
items.summary: U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres announced a proposed bill that would direct the FTC to protect consumers who buy digital games, potentially requiring transferable ownership rights and offline modes for games that depend on online servers. The proposal has not yet been formally introduced and has no scheduled vote.

items.title: CONTROL Resonant surpasses one million sales
items.summary: Remedy Entertainment’s CONTROL Resonant has sold more than one million copies worldwide, making it the company’s fastest-selling game in its 31-year history. The game launched September 24, 2026, on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2026 nominees announced
items.summary: The 2026 Golden Joystick Awards revealed nominees spanning major releases and indie games, including Crimson Desert, DAVE THE DIVER, Big Walk, Dispatch, Mina the Hollower, Forza Horizon 6, and Resident Evil Requiem.

items.title: Xbox hiring role focused on physical game distribution
items.summary: Microsoft is recruiting a Games Supply Strategist to coordinate physical Xbox game launches, inventory, and retail execution. The opening suggests Xbox continues to plan for physical game distribution despite broader industry movement toward digital sales.

items.title: Forza Horizon 6 reportedly coming to PS5 in January 2027
items.summary: Forza Horizon 6 is scheduled to reach PlayStation 5 on January 26, 2027, according to a current multiplatform release listing.

items.title: This week’s releases include Call of Duty and Final Fantasy titles
items.summary: The week’s release schedule spans PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2, with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Final Fantasy Resonance, and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort among the highlighted launches.
